n: Joseph had prayed, “O Lord, show unto thy servants how much thou requirest of the properties of thy people for a tithing.” The answer begins: members should first give their surplus property to the bishop in Zion.

f.g: What a family had beyond its reasonable needs.

f.w: the bishop of my church in Zion

n: These funds were to build the temple, lay Zion’s foundation, support priesthood work, and pay the First Presidency’s debts.
This initial offering marks the beginning of tithing as a formal law in the restored Church.
After that first gift, members are to pay one-tenth of their “interest” each year. Church leaders have explained “interest” as income. This is a permanent law for supporting the Lord’s work.

f.w: one-tenth of all their interest annually

n: Everyone gathering to Zion must keep this law to be considered worthy to live among the Saints.

f.w: shall be tithed of their surplus properties

n: Tithing is part of how Zion becomes holy. If the Saints don’t keep it, the land will not be Zion for them—it’s the people’s hearts, not the location, that make Zion.
This law serves as an “ensample”—an example or model—for every stake.
